emergence.summary: A rare autosomal-recessive disorder of extreme hypertriglyceridaemia. Lipoprotein lipase (LPL) is the endothelial enzyme that hydrolyses triglyceride in circulating chylomicrons and VLDL -- functionally a BRAKE that keeps plasma triglyceride low by clearing it. Biallelic LPL loss-of-function (the commonest cause; GPIHBP1, APOA5, LMF1, APOC2 give the same syndrome) RELEASES that brake, so chylomicrons are not cleared and plasma triglyceride over-accumulates -- the emergent lipid-metabolite axis is driven UP (fasting chylomicronaemia, recurrent acute pancreatitis, eruptive xanthomata, lipaemia retinalis). This is read with the released-brake -> downstream over-accumulation pattern already used for the toxic-metabolite diseases (tyrosinaemia, porphyria, hyperoxaluria, OTC), now carried onto a NEW lipid metabolite -- triglyceride -- and is the OPPOSITE mode to familial hypercholesterolaemia, where the defect is loss of LDL-cholesterol clearance read on the level-restore (axis-DOWN) side. Because the axis is driven UP, the corrective direction is to RESTRAIN it. The lead lever the switch re-derives is to RESTRAIN apolipoprotein C-III (APOC3): ApoC-III is an endogenous INHIBITOR of LPL, so lowering it DE-REPRESSES LPL and restores triglyceride clearance -- the approved hepatocyte-targeted APOC3 antisense oligonucleotide olezarsen, and the EU-approved APOC3 ASO volanesorsen, both act this way (the APOC3-siRNA plozasiran is late-stage clinical). Restoring LPL itself (gene therapy) is recorded as a restrain-coded lever because its NET effect on the emergent triglyceride axis is DOWN (the OTC net-effect convention); alipogene tiparvovec, an AAV1-LPL gene therapy, was historically the first gene therapy approved in the Western world (EMA 2012) and was later commercially withdrawn, so current LPL gene-therapy programmes are investigational. Conventional very-low-fat diet and fibrates/omega-3 are recorded as supportive / largely ineffective in true LPL-null FCS and are NOT switch levers. The gamma read is of the LPL promoter switch STRUCTURE; the disease lesions are coding (e.g. LPL p.Gly188Glu, p.Asp9Asn), outside the promoter firewall. Magnitude [O].

per_gene.note: LPL encodes lipoprotein lipase, the endothelial-surface enzyme (anchored via GPIHBP1) that hydrolyses core triglyceride in chylomicrons and VLDL, clearing plasma triglyceride. It is the physiological BRAKE on circulating triglyceride. Biallelic LOF (null/severe-hypomorph) abolishes clearance -> the brake is released -> the triglyceride axis is pushed UP (fasting chylomicronaemia). Located 8p21.3 (OMIM 609708). NCBI official symbol LPL. Autosomal recessive. Coding lesions (e.g. p.Gly188Glu founder allele; p.Asp9Asn); promoter firewall respected.

falsifiers.claim: biallelic LPL loss-of-function raises the plasma-triglyceride axis (releases the clearance brake)
falsifiers.falsifier: an LPL null/severe-LOF genotype that LOWERED fasting plasma triglyceride, or restoration of LPL activity that RAISED it, refutes the released-brake (axis-UP) direction
falsifiers.measurable_by: post-heparin plasma LPL activity versus fasting plasma triglyceride, stratified by LPL genotype

falsifiers.claim: lowering ApoC-III is the CORRECTIVE direction (de-represses LPL -> lowers triglyceride)
falsifiers.falsifier: if reducing ApoC-III RAISED plasma triglyceride or failed to accelerate chylomicron clearance, the restrain-APOC3 lever sign is wrong
falsifiers.measurable_by: fasting plasma triglyceride and chylomicron clearance response to an APOC3-lowering oligonucleotide in FCS
